rem:information-causality:
Remark Information causality and the light cone. One places the quantum observable universe (QOU) within information-theoretic physics. The energy \mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{m}\,c_q^2 (mass--energy equivalence) and the derived speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) connect the QOU to established information bounds.

1. The light cone is the Lieb--Robinson cone. The causal boundary arises from the q-connection decomposition A_q = q^{-1}A + \hbar_q\iota_\xi A\varTheta. The boundary at |Z| = c_q in the contact affine coordinate (contact affine chart) is the locus where horizontal spatial diffusion matches vertical Reeb advance. Outside this cone, the Lieb--Robinson bound enforces exponential suppression of correlations. Causality follows directly from the ratio of spatial to temporal information flow.

2. The speed of light varies with q. The speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) depends on the substrate parameter. At the Big Bang (q \to \infty), c \to 0. As the universe classicalises (q \to 1), c \to \infty. At the present epoch q = q_0, c \approx 9.093 in Reeb units.

3. The Margolus--Levitin bound and c_q. The Margolus--Levitin theorem of Norman Margolus and Lev B. Levitin [margolus1998] bounds the orthogonal-state transition rate by 2\mathfrak{E}/\pi\hbar [lloyd2000]. One has the energy \mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{m}\,c_q^2 = \mathfrak{m}/(q-1)^2 and the operation count n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q. The bound is:

  n_R(q)  \leq  \frac{2\mathfrak{m}}{\pi\hbar_q(q-1)^2}.

The Reeb dynamics saturates this bound up to the factor 2/\pi.

4. Bremermann's limit and information bandwidth. Bremermann's limit, evaluated as a mass-energy ceiling on physical computation by Seth Lloyd [lloyd2000], states that a system processes at most mc^2/h bits per second. The bandwidth is:

  \mathfrak{B}(q)
  =  \frac{q\eta_q}{(q-1)^2}
  \quad \text{(\(q\)-bits per Planck time)}.

At q = q_0, \mathcal{B} \approx 82 q-bits per Planck time.

5. Pawlowski's information causality. Information causality [pawlowski2009] restricts the accessible information Bob gains from Alice. In the QOU, the Lieb--Robinson bound ensures exponential decay outside the |Z| = c_q cone.

6. The Bekenstein bound and fibre entropy. The Bekenstein bound of Jacob D. Bekenstein [bekenstein1981] limits the entropy to S \leq 2\pi RE / \hbar c. One bounds the QOU fibre entropy by \eta_q per operation:

  S_{\mathrm{fibre}}  \leq  \eta_q
  =  \frac{2q - 1}{q^3}.

7. Summary. Every classical information and computation bound above [lloyd2000] descends from two substrate quantities: the causal cone |Z| = c_q with c_q = 1/(q-1), and the per-operation fibre-entropy ceiling \eta_q = (2q - 1)/q^3. The cone fixes the Lieb--Robinson / information-causality light cone and the q-dependent speed of light; the entropy ceiling caps the Margolus--Levitin operation rate, the Bremermann bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q), and the Bekenstein entropy. Causality, processing rate, and entropy are thus one q-parametrised family.

sec:optical-fibre-intro:
To model the physical transmission of information, one introduces the one-dimensional channel. This construct represents an optical fibre acting as a one-dimensional waveguide. This physical "fibre" is distinct from the categorical fibre functor \tau.

A channel transmits information by carrying a braid word \beta \in B_n along its length. The measurable output of this transmission is the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta). The fibre is bounded by its cladding, a topological boundary that prevents strands from crossing the surface. This boundary strictly isolates the interior braid. Consequently, adjacent fibres decouple into a split configuration. The joint Markov trace of parallel fibres factorizes into the product of their individual traces. The total information capacity thus derives from the operational entropy of the substrate.
def:one-dim-qou-channel:
Definition One-dimensional QOU channel (optical fibre). Structural; holds over a generic commutative ring R.

A one-dimensional channel over a commutative ring R is a bounded braid carrier along a line, conveying a braid word \beta \in B_n. The transmitted datum is the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) \in R.

The cladding is a topological boundary condition that confines \beta so that no strand crosses the boundary surface. A channel is determined by its trace value. The vacuum channel is the empty fibre with \beta = \mathbf{1} and \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}) = 1.

This channel structure includes the vacuum channel and the parallel placement of two side-by-side fibres:

  \mathcal{F}_A \parallel \mathcal{F}_B := \langle\, \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{F}_A)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{F}_B) \,\rangle .

This product relies on the multiplicativity of the Markov trace over split links, as parallel cladded fibres decouple.
prop:parallel-fibre-noninteraction:
Proposition Parallel placement of one-dimensional channels forms a commutative monoid. Structural; holds over a generic commutative ring R.

Model a one-dimensional channel by its transmitted datum, a single trace value \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{F}) \in R, and define the parallel placement \mathcal{F}_A \parallel \mathcal{F}_B as the channel whose trace is the product

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{F}_A \parallel \mathcal{F}_B) \;:=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{F}_A)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{F}_B).

Then parallel placement is associative and commutative, and the vacuum channel (trace 1) is a two-sided identity. Channels under parallel placement form a commutative monoid.

The product rule is the definition of \parallel here, not a consequence. Its physical motivation is that cladding makes the joint configuration a split link, and the Markov trace is multiplicative over split links; that link-level argument is not part of this statement.
prf:parallel-fibre-noninteraction: Proof Proof of parallel fibre noninteraction. One obtains the factorisation directly from the split-link multiplicativity of the Markov trace. This is equivalent to the disjoint-union rule for the Kauffman bracket and the Jones polynomial. Associativity, commutativity, and the identity law follow from the corresponding ring identities for the product of trace values. All four properties hold over a generic commutative ring R. The factorisation is definitional. \qquad\blacksquare
rem:fibre-channel-capacity:
Remark Information capacity of a fibre as Markov-trace entropy. Interpretation of the one-dimensional channel.

Information is encoded in the braid word \beta and read out via the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta). Braid words sharing the same trace are indistinguishable to the receiver. The capacity of the channel is the entropy of the reachable trace image. It counts the distinguishable values of \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) rather than the raw braids.

An elementary crossing provides at most the operational entropy \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3. The capacity of an n-strand fibre carrying a length-\ell braid is bounded by \ell\,\eta_q q-bits. This bound constitutes a one-dimensional analogue of the Bekenstein and Bremermann limits.

Because parallel fibres do not interact, their joint Markov trace multiplies and their capacities add. A bundle of k independent fibres carries exactly k times the single-fibre capacity. This mirrors the classical additivity of independent information channels.
rem:photon-propagation-1d:
Remark Photon modes and q-deformed dispersion in a 1D channel. Interpretation of the one-dimensional channel.

A photon is a trivial strand \gamma, knot-trivial under Markov closure. In a fibre, it is a propagating excitation that carries no crossings as it advances. The n strands of the fibre represent its modes. A bounded fibre supports exactly n propagating modes. This gives a topological origin to waveguide mode quantization, directly analogous to the discrete mode count of a step-index fibre.

Propagation is governed by the substrate velocity c_q = 1/(q-1). The dispersion of a mode is the q-deformation of its propagation eigenvalue. A mode of wavenumber k advances with the q-integer phase [k]_q rather than the classical k. The group velocity thus acquires O(1 - q^{-1}) corrections. In the rigid, lossless limit of a straight fibre, these corrections reduce to linear dispersion.

This energy-dependent mode velocity manifests in-vacuo dispersion at the channel level. It aligns with doubly-special-relativity phenomenology and is constrained by gamma-ray-burst bounds on archimedean deformation residues.
rem:dsr-planck-scale-phenomenology:
Remark Doubly special relativity and Planck-scale phenomenology: kinship and constraints for c_q. Interpretation of the information speed of light.

The derived light speed c_q = 1/(q-1) and the O(1 - q^{-1}) group-velocity corrections induced by the q-integer phase [k]_q on photon modes (photon modes) locate this framework within the lineage of doubly special relativity (DSR) and Planck-scale phenomenology. This literature provides both a structural precedent and the sharpest experimental constraints.

Structural kinship with DSR. Amelino-Camelia's testable minimum-length scenario [amelinocamelia2001] introduces a second observer-independent scale—a Planckian length—alongside the speed of light. It deforms the photon dispersion relation at first order in the ratio of the photon's energy to a quantum-gravity scale \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{QG}}. A quantum-group (\kappa-Poincaré) structure, rather than the classical Poincaré algebra, realizes the deformed symmetry.

The QOU substrate mirrors this construction. The deformation parameter q acts as the Planckian invariant. Macroscopic Lorentz covariance emerges only after the archimedean projection. In both frameworks, the photon velocity is energy-dependent at the deformed level. In DSR this occurs through the modified dispersion relation; here, it occurs through the q-integer phase [k]_q replacing the classical wavenumber k. The DSR precedent proves that an observer-independent deformation scale is compatible with a relativity principle and avoids a preferred frame. The local substrate q_0 should enter the archimedean layer as a second invariant, not as a frame-dependent violation.

Experimental constraints. Time-of-flight tests on gamma-ray bursts probe the Planck scale [amelinocamelia1998]. The Fermi observation of GRB 090510 [abdo2009] excludes photon dispersion linear in the energy ratio up to a quantum-gravity scale exceeding the Planck energy. The surrounding observational programme is surveyed in [amelinocamelia2013].

Prima facie, the substrate values strongly conflict with these bounds. A fractional dispersion of order \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} surviving to astrophysical photon propagation would exceed the GRB limits by many orders of magnitude. To maintain consistency, the q-deformed dispersion must remain confined to the substrate (fibre) level. The archimedean projection must suppress its residue at accessible energies. The framework does not currently derive this suppression scale. This is the sharpest falsifiability exposure of the dispersive prediction. An eventual substrate-to-archimedean dispersion calculation must guarantee that any archimedean residue of the [k]_q phase falls below the GRB 090510 limit [abdo2009].

prf:toffoli-transfer-matrix:
Proof Proof of toffoli transfer matrix. On 3 strands, the chain reduction (transfer matrix product) produces two generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1 with traced volumes \hat{V}_0(q), \hat{V}_1(q).

Single-crossing type-blindness (key lemma). Generator \sigma_1 contains one crossing (strand 1 with strand 2). The traced volume is \hat{V}_1 = z \cdot c + d, where (c, d) depends on the crossing type. Direct computation yields:

  \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{pp})} = z \cdot 1 + 0 = z
  \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{mix})}
  = z \cdot 1 - \tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2}
  = z - \tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2}
  \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{nn})}
  = z \cdot 1 - (q - q^{-1})
  = z - (q - q^{-1})

These three values are not equal. They differ in the d coefficient. A single crossing therefore carries type information: \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{mix})} - \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{pp})} = -\tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2} and \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{nn})} - \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{pp})} = -(q - q^{-1}).

What vanishes is the target-flip difference, not the type dependence. Generator \sigma_1 operates on strands 1 and 2. This is the control–control crossing. A target-flip acts on strand 3, leaving strands 1 and 2 unchanged. Parent and daughter therefore carry the same \sigma_1 crossing type, hence the same \hat{V}_1. This forces:

  \Delta_1 = \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{par})} - \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{dau})} = 0

for every target-flip transition. This occurs because the control crossing is fixed, not because \hat{V}_1 is type-independent.

Target-flip amplitude. Since \Delta_1 = 0, the 1-jet formula reduces to:

  P_{\mathrm{flip}} = \hat{V}_1 \cdot \Delta_0
  = z \cdot \bigl(\hat{V}_0^{(\mathrm{par})} -
    \hat{V}_0^{(\mathrm{dau})}\bigr)

The chain at \sigma_0 contains two crossings: (0,1) and (0,2). The target flip changes the (0,2) crossing type but leaves the (0,1) crossing unchanged. Chain reduction gives \hat{V}_0 = z \cdot a_0 + b_0, where a_0, b_0 depend on both crossings. The difference \Delta_0 factors. The unchanged (0,1) crossing contributes its coefficient c_{01} as a prefactor. The changing (0,2) crossing contributes the same core difference regardless of the (0,1) type.

Therefore \Delta_0 = c_{01} \cdot \Delta_{02}(q), where c_{01} = 1 is the crossing coefficient of the control–control pair and \Delta_{02} is the core difference at the changing crossing. However, in P_{\mathrm{flip}} = \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{par})}\,\Delta_0, the prefactor \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{par})} = z + d_{01} varies across the three control pairs \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{p}, mixed, and \mathfrak{n}\mathfrak{n} through d_{01} \in \{0, -\tfrac{q-q^{-1}}{2}, -(q-q^{-1})\}, yielding the three distinct values of item 2 rather than a single control-independent amplitude.

All-proton q-AND and reverse flip. For the all-proton control pair (c_{01}, d_{01}) = (1, 0), substituting z = q^3/(q^2+1) gives

  P_{7,6}(q) = -\,\frac{(q-1)(q+1)\bigl(q^{6} + q^{4} + 2q^{2} + 1\bigr)}{2q\,(q^{2}+1)^{2}},

establishing item 3. Evaluating the reverse transition from its own parent input column replaces the sextic factor by 2q^6 + q^4 + q^2 + 1, giving P_{6,7}(q) \neq -P_{7,6}(q) (item 4).

Classical limit. At q = 1, q - q^{-1} = 0, so all crossing types coincide and \Delta_0 = 0; every target-flip amplitude carries the factor (q - 1) (item 5).

Toffoli diagonals. For the all-proton ordering every crossing has (c, d) = (1, 0), so \hat{V}_1 = z and \hat{V}_0 = 1 + (q - q^{-1})z, giving P_{7,7}(q) = \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1 = z + (q - q^{-1})z^2. Substituting z = q^3/(q^2+1) yields P_{7,7}(q) = q^3(q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, and the analogous product on the even parity sector yields P_{6,6}(q) = (q^4+1)(q^4+q^2+2)/\bigl(4q(q^2+1)^2\bigr), both strictly positive on (0,\infty) (item 6). \square

In the classical Toffoli gate (CCNOT), the target bit flips if and only if both control bits are 1. Three Planck steps. The 3-strand Toffoli braid contains \binom{3}{2} = 3 crossings. A single crossing is not a complete topological operation; one must close the full braid loop. The complete Toffoli gate therefore executes in exactly 3 Planck steps, allocating one step per crossing.

Any irreversible Turing machine can be simulated by a reversible one relying entirely on Toffoli gates, with at most polynomial overhead in time and space. Combined with a single-qubit gate outside the Clifford group, the Toffoli gate achieves quantum computational universality. Since P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0 for every q \neq 1, the substrate's braiding dynamics, operating in discrete Planck steps, is computationally universal away from the classical limit.

  1. (The operator threshold.) The derived family has a single threshold on (0,\infty): See Table 1.   2. (Dual shadow prices.) For q > 1, the LP dual admits bounded shadow prices y_i^*(q) satisfying:

where \kappa(\mathrm{G}(q)) = \lambda_{\max}(G)/|\lambda_{\min}(G)|. Open boundary (Gram radical). Because y_{(1^3)} = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the Markov–Gram form on H_3(q) is singular, so \lambda_{\max}/|\lambda_{\min}| in the ordinary sense is infinite on the full six-dimensional normal-form span; formulating a finite shadow-price bound requires passing to the quotient by the radical, as in Term 4 of the six-term mass identity.

  1. (Physical-substrate stability — the positivity reduction does not hold as stated.) At q_0 \approx 1.110 (with z = q^3/(q^2+1)):

  P_{7,6}(q_0) \,\approx\, -0.1438.

Two qualifications, both of which bound what that is worth. First, the Gram is entrywise non-negative, and \vec t is too for the all-proton ordering, so for that ordering positivity is forced by shape with no cancellation possible — 2 of the 8 orderings are trivial in this sense and 6 are not. Second, and more consequential: \vec t acquires a negative component exactly when \hbar_\times < 0, i.e. on 0 < q < 1 — the opposite side of q = 1 from where P_{7,6} is negative. The amplitude sign and the cone condition disagree about which regime is the admissible one, so the reduction above does not merely mix index spaces.

That sign inversion is now proved to be an identity, and it excludes the reduction as written. Since \hbar_\times = (q-1)(q+1)/q, the flip amplitude factors as

  P_{7,6}(q) \;=\; -\,\hbar_\times\,\cdot\,\frac{S(q)}{2(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad S(q) = q^6+q^4+2q^2+1,

and S has no real root while (q^2+1)^2 > 0, so the cofactor is strictly positive on all of \mathbb{R}. This is proved, with an independent symbolic cross-check.

This is a scope-(b) exclusion, and the invariant is the factorisation above: no reduction in which the cone condition inherits the flip amplitude's sign can hold at any q > 0, because the two carry exactly opposite signs of the same factor. It does not exclude a reduction carrying a negative proportionality — one in which the cone condition follows -P_{7,6} — and that is the natural remaining candidate.

No claim of LP-instability is made, and none is available: the condition as stated is satisfied. The downstream statement that \{q\text{-Toffoli}, H\} generates universal reversible computation on the Reeb bundles inherits that opening.

The reduction is refuted by a zero-set argument. The proof reduces the cone condition to P_{7,7}W_{\mathrm{std}} "with the appropriate sign from" P_{7,6}. The numerator is irreducible over \mathbb{Q} and has exactly one positive real root, matching the bisected threshold to 1.14\times10^{-46}. Proved without the intermediate value theorem and without q_c's value: across [1/2, 9/10] the cone constraint changes sign while both claimed factors stay strictly positive at each endpoint.

Why the reduction had to fail: the relation exists, but at degree 2. The eight amplitudes generate the whole field \mathbb{Q}(q) — four of them reconstruct q itself, via M_{33}/M_{44} = q^4 and P_{7,7}/M_{00} = q^6 — so asking whether the cone condition is some rational expression in them has no content. Restricting the form does. Over the common denominator q^6(q^2+1)^4 the ambient space of numerators is 21-dimensional, and the degree-2 span of the amplitudes has rank 15: a proper subspace of codimension 6, which a generic rational function does not meet. The cone constraint is in it, and four amplitudes already suffice:

\[

  \;+\; \tfrac{5}{36}M_{00}^2 \;-\; \tfrac{20}{3}M_{00}M_{33} \;-\; \tfrac{10}{9}M_{00}M_{44} \;+\; \tfrac{5}{18}M_{00}P_{7,7} \\

This identity is proved, together with the transfer of sign from the numerator to the constraint. Only + and \times appear: no division by an amplitude, hence no reconstruction of q. The cross terms are load-bearing — the span of the amplitudes and their squares alone has rank 14 and does not contain the constraint.

This sharpens the refutation rather than softening it. A monomial vanishes exactly where a factor does; a degree-2 polynomial can vanish where none of its terms does, and that is precisely the mechanism producing the root at q_c. So the published reduction was the right kind of relation in the wrong class: it needed cancellation between products, which a single product cannot supply. Whether any member of the (one-parameter) solution family has a Hecke-theoretic reading is open.

The natural coordinates are the Markov and Hecke parameters, and there the expression is forced. The rational coefficients above are a fact about the amplitude basis, not about the constraint. Writing z = q^3/(q^2+1) for the Markov parameter and \hbar_\times = q - 1/q for the Hecke deformation of \sigma^2 = \hbar_\times\sigma + 1,

  (G\vec t)_5 \;=\; z^2 \;+\; 2\hbar_\times z \;+\; 3\hbar_\times^2 z^2 \;+\; \hbar_\times^3 z \;+\; \hbar_\times^4 z^2 ,

with integer coefficients (1,2,3,1,1) and no denominators. Degree 6 is minimal — no polynomial in (z,\hbar_\times) of total degree \leq 5 equals it — and minimal degree is a genuine invariant of the class. The polynomial identity is proved.

The coefficient string, however, is not an invariant. The two parameters are algebraically dependent, satisfying the irreducible degree-4 relation

so \mathbb{Q}[z,\hbar_\times] is not a polynomial ring but the coordinate ring of an affine rational curve, and a polynomial representative is unique only modulo that relation. This is forced, not fitted. Every Markov trace of a Hecke word lies in \mathbb{Z}[z,\hbar_\times] — the Markov property \mathrm{tr}(x\sigma_{\mathrm{last}}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}(x) removes the highest generator and the quadratic relation reduces the rest — and in particular \hbar_\times z^2 + z = \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0). Since the q-Toffoli's normal-form coordinates are \vec t = (0,0,1,\hbar_\times,0,0), that is T_q = \sigma_1 + \hbar_\times\sigma_0\sigma_1, the constraint (G\vec t)_5 = \mathrm{tr}(W\sigma_1) + \hbar_\times\mathrm{tr}(W\sigma_0\sigma_1) lies in \mathbb{Z}[z,\hbar_\times] before any computation is done.

Both parameters are needed: the constraint's minimal polynomial over \mathbb{Q}(z) has degree 3 and over \mathbb{Q}(\hbar_\times) degree 2, so it is a function of neither alone. Since those degrees are coprime, \mathbb{Q}(z,\hbar_\times) = \mathbb{Q}(q) and the content is the subring statement, not a field one. Separately, the numerator is neither reciprocal nor anti-reciprocal, so it is the Alexander polynomial of no knot — a scope-(b) exclusion resting on the reciprocity invariant.

The Gram matrix G over H_3(q) has a characteristic polynomial whose eigenvalue crossings are controlled by the discriminant of the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0. The smallest eigenvalue \lambda_{\min}(\mathrm{G}(q)) is continuous in q. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the bilinear pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) carries one negative eigenvalue, \lambda_{\min}(q_0) = -0.75270211 (with a one-dimensional radical from y_{(1^3)} = 0), whereas on the star pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j^*) the form is positive semidefinite with signature (5,0,1). Write T_q in the NF basis. The target-flip amplitude P_{7,6}(q) determines the off-diagonal mass component. The diagonal P_{7,7}(q) determines the Wedderburn weight of the standard channel (Toffoli transfer matrix). Positivity of G\vec{t}(q) therefore reduces to the positivity of the product P_{7,7}(q) \cdot W_{\mathrm{std}}(q) with the appropriate sign from the off-diagonal amplitude.

Open step — the second half of the reduction is underived. The derived off-diagonal amplitude is

  P_{7,6}(q) \;=\; -\frac{(q-1)(q+1)(q^6+q^4+2q^2+1)}{2q(q^2+1)^2}

(Toffoli transfer matrix). The reduction above is asserted in a single clause and the part that carries the weight — "with the appropriate sign from" the off-diagonal amplitude — is not derived: nothing states what that sign must be, or why. The first factor satisfies P_{7,7}(q)\,W_{\mathrm{std}}(q) > 0 for all q > 0; the second is open.

Solving P_{7,7}(q) = 0 on (0,\infty): the numerator is q^3(q^4+1), whose only real zero is q = 0, so the derived diagonal has no positive zero.

Solving P_{7,6}(q) = 0 on (0,\infty): the factor (q-1) gives q = 1; the factor (q+1) has no positive root; and q^6 + q^4 + 2q^2 + 1 > 0 for every real q. So q = 1 is the only positive zero.

For q > 1: P_{7,7}(q) > 0 but P_{7,6}(q) < 0, since the sextic factor is positive and the sign is carried by -(q-1)(q+1). The Wedderburn weights W_{\mathrm{sym}} = W_{\mathrm{alt}} = q^2/(q^4 + 4q^2 + 1) and W_{\mathrm{std}} = (q^2+1)^2/(q^4 + 4q^2 + 1) are strictly positive. So the sign pattern on the physical regime is mixed, not uniformly positive: the amplitudes of the derived family are not all of the same sign. Whether linear reduction preserves feasibility under a mixed pattern is the open step above; item 4 of the proposition evaluates G\vec t(q_0) directly instead.

For 0 < q < 1: P_{7,6}(q) > 0. The sign reversal of the off-diagonal amplitude occurs at q = 1 and nowhere else.

The boundedness of shadow prices is not a consequence of LP duality (LP-dual stability states only feasibility and strong duality). The bound used here is the one recorded in the confinement reading: the dual norm |y^*| bounded by the primal norm times the Gram condition number \kappa(\mathrm{G}(q)) = \lambda_{\max}(G)/|\lambda_{\min}(G)|. Open step (Gram singularity). At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Markov–Gram form is singular (y_{(1^3)} = 0), so the ratio \lambda_{\max}/|\lambda_{\min}| is not a finite condition number on the full six-dimensional normal-form span. Moreover, at q_0, P_{7,7}(q_0) \approx 0.6912 > 0 whereas P_{7,6}(q_0) \approx -0.1438 < 0. Closing the shadow-price bound requires passing to the quotient by the radical, and closing the amplitude step requires deriving the off-diagonal sign relation. \square

Proposition The quantum Game of Life (q-GoL) as a Toffoli-defined substrate automaton. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q and Planck time t_P(q) = 1/\hbar_q. Let \mathcal{L} \subset M be a discrete sublattice of brane points \{p_i\}. Each site carries a qubit |\psi_i\rangle \in \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. The q-Game of Life (q-GoL) is the discrete-time invertible cellular automaton

  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
    \colon  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}}
    \to  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}},
  \qquad
  |\Psi(t{+}1)\rangle
   = 
  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
  |\Psi(t)\rangle.

The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is constructed entirely from q-deformed Toffoli gates acting on Reeb bundle fibres of neighbour sites. The construction requires five properties:

  1. Building block. The transition operator is the q-AND gate:
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \colon  |c_1, c_2, t\rangle
  \longmapsto
  |c_1, c_2,  t \oplus_q (c_1 \wedge_q c_2)\rangle.

The symbol \wedge_q denotes the Hecke-algebra q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q), given under Well-definedness condition below. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q executes in three Planck steps.

No control-independent factor \Phi(q) lies in the image of the three-strand Toffoli construction (Toffoli transfer matrix); \wedge_q is evaluated directly via P_{7,6}(q).

  1. Superposition. Cell states admit superpositions |\psi_i\rangle = \alpha_i|0\rangle + \beta_i|1\rangle via Hadamard rotations H \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{S}_{p_i}). The set \{\mathrm{Toff}_q, H\} is universal for reversible computation, in the sense of Bennett, for every q > 0: reversible universality needs the gate to be invertible with a firing target-flip channel, both of which item 4 and the non-vanishing of P_{7,6} on q \neq 1 supply.

Scope of universality. The standard Toffoli-plus-Hadamard quantum universality theorem applies to unitary gates, whereas \mathrm{Toff}_q is provably not unitary for q \neq 1. Whether a non-unitary invertible gate set can be universal in a quantum sense is unsettled, so item 2 states reversible universality only.

  1. Conway's rules as Toffoli circuits. Survival (k = 2, 3) and birth (k = 3) at site i with neighbourhood N(i) are enacted by the composite operator
  \mathcal{U}_i^{\mathrm{rule}}
   = 
  \prod_{\{j_1, j_2\} \subset N(i)}
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \!\left(
    |\psi_{j_1}\rangle,  |\psi_{j_2}\rangle;  |\psi_i\rangle
  \right).

Ancilla qubits encode the neighbour sum. A ripple-carry adder of O(|N(i)|) Toffoli gates computes the binary count k.

  1. Reversibility. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q is invertible, with
  \sigma_i^{-1}
   = 
  \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot \mathbb{1},

so \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is invertible and the automaton is reversible. It is not unitary away from the classical limit: the eigenvalues of \sigma_i are q and -q^{-1}, of modulus \neq 1 for q \neq 1, so no inner product makes \mathrm{Toff}_q unitary, and the Markov trace form has a nontrivial radical at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Reversibility in the sense a reversible cellular automaton requires — invertibility of the tick — therefore holds for every q > 0, being a property of the quadratic relation alone and independent of the amplitude signs discussed below; unitarity holds only at q = 1.

  1. Information bandwidth budget. One generation advances in 3 |\mathcal{L}| Planck steps. The substrate bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) = q \eta_q / (q - 1)^2 bounds the generation rate:
  \text{gens / sec}
   \leq 
  \frac{\mathfrak{B}(q)}{3  |\mathcal{L}|}
   = 
  \frac{q \eta_q}{3  (q - 1)^2  |\mathcal{L}|}.

Well-definedness condition. The evolution is well-defined only when the Toffoli diagonal P_{7,7}(q) is positive and the q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q) is non-zero. With Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the two amplitudes are

  P_{7,7}(q) \,=\, \frac{q^{3}\bigl(q^{4}+1\bigr)}{\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}},
  \qquad
  P_{7,6}(q) \,=\, -\,\frac{(q-1)(q+1)\bigl(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1\bigr)}{2q\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}}.

For q > 0 the first is strictly positive, having no positive root. The second vanishes exactly at q = 1: the factor (q+1) is positive there, and the sextic q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1 has no positive real root, so the whole zero set on q > 0 is carried by (q-1). The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the substrate value q_0 \approx 1.110.

Non-vanishing, not positivity. The criterion is that the q-AND does not degenerate, not that it carry a particular sign. This is the same condition the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND uses — it turns on P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0 — and it is what invertibility of the tick requires. At q = 1 the q-AND vanishes and the braiding ceases to act: that is the classical limit, where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli, and it is the one point the condition excludes.

Strict positivity would be a different and stronger requirement: at z = q^3/(q^2+1) it holds only on 0 < q < 1, since P_{7,6}(q_0) \approx -0.1438, and would place the substrate outside the well-defined regime. It is not the criterion in force here.

Direct LP feasibility vs. amplitude sign. Constructing the q-Toffoli as an element of H_3(q) — T_q = \sigma_1 + \hbar_\times\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 for the all-proton ordering — and evaluating the LP condition G\vec t(q_0) \geq 0 directly against the H_3(q) Markov–Gram matrix gives strictly positive components for all eight strand-type orderings (Toffoli LP-stability). Thus the substrate satisfies LP feasibility as well as non-vanishing. Two structural properties qualify this: first, the Gram matrix is entrywise non-negative and \vec t is entrywise non-negative for the all-proton ordering, so positivity is forced by shape for 2 of the 8 orderings and nontrivial for the remaining 6; second, \vec t turns negative on 0 < q < 1, the opposite side of q = 1 from where P_{7,6}(q) < 0, so the amplitude sign and the LP cone condition select opposite regimes.

Proof Proof of q game of life. The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is built from q-Toffoli generators. By Toffoli transfer matrix, these act as elements of H_3(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes H_3(q) on the tensor product of Reeb bundles \bigotimes_i \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. Each generator is invertible in H_n(q), and it is invertibility — not unitarity — that this argument establishes. For real q > 0 with q \neq 1, the eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i have modulus \neq 1, so \sigma_i is not unitary with respect to any positive-definite inner product (by contrast, Squier's invariant bar-Hermitian form over \mathbb{Z}[s, s^{-1}] with s^2 = t is indefinite away from the unit circle [squier1984, Theorem, p. 199; \S 3, eq. (6), p. 201]); and the Markov trace form is not available as a Hilbert inner product on H_n(q), having a nontrivial radical at z = q^3/(q^2+1) for n \ge 3. Reversibility therefore rests on invertibility alone: the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 gives the explicit inverse

  \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot 1 ,

so every \sigma_i is a unit and the composite is invertible. The generators are not involutions at generic q: \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i holds precisely when q = q^{-1}, i.e. in the classical limit q \to 1, which is where the q-Toffoli reduces to the ordinary Toffoli gate.

Any reversible computation is simulated by Toffoli gates [bennett1973, toffoli1980, fredkin1982]. That Toffoli together with Hadamard is universal for quantum computation is the theorem of Shi and of Aharonov [shi2002, aharonov2003], stated for the standard Toffoli gate; its extension to \mathrm{Toff}_q at q \neq 1 is not established here.

The bandwidth bound follows by counting. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q in the 3-strand Hecke algebra requires three elementary crossings, taking three Planck steps. One generation applies one Toffoli gate per neighbour triple. This yields the stated bound.

The well-definedness condition requires P_{7,7}(q) > 0 and P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the diagonal is P_{7,7}(q) = q^{3}(q^{4}+1)/(q^{2}+1)^{2}; numerator and denominator are strictly positive for every q > 0, so the first clause holds throughout and places no constraint. The q-AND is P_{7,6}(q) = -(q-1)(q+1)(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1)/\bigl(2q(q^{2}+1)^{2}\bigr); for q > 0 the factor (q+1) is positive and the sextic has no positive real root, so the zero set is exactly \{q = 1\} and the second clause holds on q \neq 1. The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the substrate. \square

Note that the criterion used here is non-vanishing, not positivity: invertibility of the tick and the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND require only P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. Strict positivity would restrict to 0 < q < 1 and exclude the substrate.
rem:q-game-of-life-interpretation:
Remark Deterministic cellular-automaton models of Peña et al. and 't Hooft. Peña et al. construct a reversible quantum Game of Life using Toffoli-based adder circuits. Their Toffoli gate is the classical limit q \to 1 of the q-Toffoli, and their construction is recovered in that limit; away from it the two are not comparable, since the q-deformed generator is invertible but not unitary. Their unitary tick maps to 3 Planck steps. One identifies the q-deformed amplitude P_{7,6}(q) as the physical AND amplitude. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) it has a single zero on q > 0, at q = 1, and the diagonal P_{7,7}(q) has none. The well-definedness condition — the diagonal positive and the q-AND non-vanishing — therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the substrate; the one excluded point is the classical limit itself, where the q-deformation contributes nothing.

The relation to 't Hooft's proposal — that quantum mechanics emerges from a deterministic Planck-scale cellular automaton — is more limited, and the limitation is structural rather than a matter of detail. The mechanism 't Hooft relies on is that a deterministic evolution permutes a distinguished basis of ontological states, so that the operator it induces on the span of that basis is automatically unitary and generates a Schrödinger flow. That step requires unitarity of the tick, and by the statement's item 4 the q-Toffoli is unitary only at q = 1.

Consequently the identification holds at q = 1 and is not established away from it. At q = 1 the tick is a permutation of basis states, the ontological states may be read as Reeb bundle fibres \mathcal{S}_p and the tick as the Planck step t_P(q) — but q = 1 is also where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli gate, so what the classical limit realizes is the construction of Peña et al. rather than anything the q-deformation contributes. At q \neq 1 the tick remains invertible, and the automaton remains deterministic and reversible in the sense a cellular automaton requires, but the induced operator is not unitary and 't Hooft's embedding does not apply as stated. Whether a deterministic automaton with an invertible non-unitary tick can support the emergence 't Hooft argues for is not addressed here.

The reading of the Markov trace as a categorical coarse-graining replacing 't Hooft's information loss is likewise not established. It is a suggestion the degeneracy of the trace form makes worth examining — a degenerate form has a radical, and quotienting by a radical is a loss of information rather than an ad hoc postulate of one — but no such identification is derived in this paper.

rem:skein-turing-machine:

sec:p-vs-np-boundary-intro:
The jet horizon isolates degree-0 data from degree \geq 1 leakage. Concurrently, the Skein Turing machine encodes every decision problem as a braid closure. Uniting these concepts maps the answer of an NP-complete decision problem to a degree-0 section of the resolution tree, while polynomial-time witnesses correspond to degree-1 paths. The gap between them constitutes a jet horizon of purely complexity-theoretic origin.

Transplanting the jet horizon onto the Skein resolution tree \mathcal{R}(L) defines the computational horizon. The Skein resolution obstruction \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}}(L, q) measures the obstruction to degree-0 evaluation via Yekutieli cohomology. Polynomial-time computation saturates the information bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) strictly below this horizon. This casts \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} as a structural claim regarding jet horizon opacity. Such degree-0 opacity parallels Hawking radiation, framing the \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} gap as information loss and computational irreversibility. This inequality localizes strictly at the non-torsion QOU substrate q \in \mathbb{G}_m.
def:computational-horizon:
Definition Computational horizon. Let L = \hat{\beta} be the braid closure of a computation \beta with c = 3N crossings encoding N Toffoli gates, let \mathcal{R}(L) be its Skein resolution tree, with 3^c leaves, and let P_L(q) be the degree-0 observable to which the Markov trace collapses \mathcal{R}(L). A computational horizon for L is a jet horizon \mathcal{H}_c \subset \mathcal{R}(L) with the following three properties.

  1. Degree-0 opacity. The evaluation P_L(q_0), which gives the yes/no answer of the decision problem, cannot be extracted from any polynomial-depth subtree of \mathcal{R}(L).
  2. Degree \geq 1 leakage. Each individual resolution path, as degree-1 linear transport data, admits verification in O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) Planck steps by checking crossing consistencies.
  3. Bandwidth saturation. With information bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) per Planck time, extracting the degree-0 answer by exploring all 3^c paths demands
  t  \geq  \frac{c \cdot \log 3}{\mathfrak{B}(q)} \cdot  3^{c - c_0}

prf:p-bandwidth-bound:
Proof Proof of p bandwidth bound. Sketch. For the forward direction, one uses the standard simulation. If a polynomial-time Turing machine decides the problem, one encodes it as a braid with c = O(\mathrm{poly}(N)) crossings. The transfer matrix product (transfer matrix) computes P_L(q) using O(c) matrix multiplications. Each multiplication costs O(1) Planck steps.

For the converse, one observes that extracting P_L(q_0) requires resolving the value of a degree \leq c^2 - 1 polynomial at a specific point. Suppose the factored form P_L(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) has O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors. Then one computes each factor in O(1) steps from the local transfer matrix, making the total cost polynomial. If the factored form requires \omega(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors, the Skein polynomial fails to compress. The information content of the computation exceeds the polynomial bandwidth budget.
rem:p-bandwidth-interpretation:

  I(t) = t \mathfrak{B}(q) = t \frac{q\eta_q}{(q-1)^2} \quad q\text{-bits.}

A \mathrm{P}-class computation succeeds when I(\mathrm{poly}(c)) suffices to determine P_L(q_0). Although the full resolution tree carries c \log_2 3 q-bits of raw information, destructive interference limits the effective content to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) q-bits, fitting within the polynomial budget.
